sentences.text:
Author: K. Lakshman
Bench: K.Lakshman, P.Sree Sudha
 The Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman
 And
 The Honourable Smt. Justice P. Sree Sudha
 Writ Petition No.8872 of 2023
Order:

(Per Honourable Sri Justice K. Lakshman) Heard Mr. M.Ratan Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner, and the learned Special Government Pleader for Home, representing the learned Additional Advocate-General, for the respondents.

2. This Writ Petition is filed by the petitioner challenging the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent vide proceedings No.18/PD-CELL/CCRB/RKD/2023, dated 18.03.2023 (for short, 'the impugned detention order') and to forthwith release the detenu, viz., Mr.Donthi Sathi Reddy (i.e.,
the father of petitioner herein).
3. Perusal of record would go to show that the impugned detention order was passed by the 2nd respondent basing on involvement of detenu in two crimes, viz., (i) Crime No.77 of 2023, for offences under Sections 420, 419, 465, 467, 468 and 471 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. on the file of P.S.
Bibinagar; and (ii) Crime No.78 of 2023, for offences under Sections 420, 419, ::2:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_8872_2023 465, 467, 468 and 471 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C. of P.S. Bibinagar.
The detenu is arrayed as Accused No.2 in the above two crimes.
4. The allegations levelled against the detenu in both the above crimes are that he along with A.1 resorted to impersonation, forgery of signatures and created certain fake documents.
The detenu is on bail in both the aforesaid crimes.

Investigating Officers did not provide material to learned Public Prosecutors to oppose the bail application, and they have not filed any application seeking cancellation of bails granted to the detenue on the ground that he had involved in similar offences.

5. It is relevant to note that this Court, vide order dated 20.06.2023 passed in Writ Petition No.8771 of 2023, had set aside the detention order passed by the 2nd respondent and also the confirmation order passed by the 1st respondent therein by declaring them as illegal, and allowed the writ Donthireddy Rajashekar Reddy vs The State Of Telangana on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105148624/
1 petition.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. In the present case, the detenu is Accused No.2 in the above two crimes and he stands on the very same footing.
Therefore, in order to maintain parity, the detenu herein is also entitled for similar relief.

Therefore, by following the order passed by this Court in Writ Petition No.8771 of 2023, dated ::3:: KL,J & PSS,J wp_8872_2023 20.06.2023, wherein this Court set forth the detenu therein, the present writ petition also deserves to be allowed on similar lines.

Accordingly, the impugned detention order passed by the 2nd respondent vide proceedings No.18/PD-CELL/CCRB/RKD/
2023, dated 18.03.2023, is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the same is set aside.
7. The writ petition is allowed.

The respondents are directed to set the detenu, viz., Donthi Sathi Reddy, S/o.Krishna Reddy, Aged : 55 years, Occ : Business, R/o.H.No.2-51/5, Raghavapur (V),
Bibinagar (M), Yadadri Bhongir District, free forthwith if he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
No costs.
8. As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending if any in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.

Note :
Issue C.C. forthwith B/o.
